title: Flight load information with context
description: For travel on non-rev tickets: see the time, the origin and the conditions behind user reports of free seats.

blocks.text: Traveling on a non-rev ticket, a person looks at the reports of a flight’s load. Two figures posted almost at the same time can contradict each other, and a confident color indicator hides that uncertainty.

quote.text: Literally received loads for 2 different airlines showing +1 and +7. Less than 10 seconds later new loads were entered showing 0 and -1. The loads are unreliable 90% of the time.

blocks.text: Next to each piece of information there should be a time, a source and the conditions it was observed in. A new entry doesn’t destroy the previous one: you can see what changed and how fresh the data is.
What decides whether it is useful

The place to start is the availability and quality of the sources, not a map of flights. User reports do not guarantee a seat on board. Without a dependable way to obtain and check fresh information, a separate product is not yet justified.
